summary: Telemetry-triggered routing to stale-kv replica intermittently causing long p99 tails and request timeouts
description:
Issue summary: Several production requests for Novalens Health routed by telemetry-based smart-routing to replicas that recently recovered from maintenance and show stale/empty KV caches. This results in intermittent long tail p99 latency (5–12s) and sporadic 504 timeouts for medium-length generation requests (max_tokens ~1024).
Impact: ~3% of requests for Novalens between 03/10 02:00–03:00 UTC experienced p99 > 6s, with ~0.4% returning 504. Customer reports degraded UX in scheduled batch jobs and interactive workspaces.
Environment: Dedicated cluster (novalens-dedicated-1) in us-east running serving-runtime v1.8.2, smart-routing agent v0.9.4, autoscaler v2.1.
Timeline:
2026-03-10 01:55 UTC: First alert from SLO monitors showing p99 spike for Novalens.
2026-03-10 02:05 UTC: Customer reports slow responses on workspace.
2026-03-10 02:12 UTC: Alerts spike; on-call alerted.
2026-03-11: Initial triage suggests fallback/variant routing coincidence with replica warmup windows.
Steps to reproduce:
1) Using Novalens test API keys, generate a medium-length request (prompt ~2K tokens) against pinned model vicuna-13b-q4f16 during a replica warmup window.
2) Observe tracing headers (x-variant, x-replica-id, x-kv-warm) returned in streaming response vectors.
3) Correlate with telemetry decisions in smart-routing logs to see preference for recently-promoted replica.
Observed behavior: smart-routing selected replicas that had recently been promoted from standby; their KV cache was cold/stale and warmup had been interrupted by concurrent canary traffic. Requests routed to these replicas saw serialization stalls while fetching KV shards and hitting disk-backed fallback, producing long p99s and occasional 504s when the request exceeded the route-level timeout.
Expected behavior: smart-routing should avoid directing production traffic to replicas that report kv_warm==false, or should route at most a tiny percentage while warmups complete.
Logs/metrics:
- Tracing snippet: "x-variant: memory-optimized-standby" "x-kv-warm: false" "route_decision: telemetry_score=0.72, recent_promotion=0.81"
- Prometheus: serving_replica_kv_miss_total spiked on replica r-1012 by 1200 in 5m.
- Router logs: "promo_event: replica r-1012 promoted at 01:39 UTC; warmup_started=01:39, warmup_progress=22% at 01:58, warmup_interrupted=true"
Temporary mitigation applied: disabled promotion-based bias in smart-routing for Novalens dedicated cluster (config flag telemetry.promote_bias=false) at 2026-03-10 03:20 UTC which reduced p99 to baseline within 20 minutes.
Next steps:
- SRE to instrument routing decision to include kv_warm flag as hard negative for traffic assignment.
- Engineering to add warmup-health-check handshake before allowing promotion to receive full traffic.
- Runbook update: add explicit check for interrupted warmups and throttled promotion windows.
investigation_notes: 03/10 02:25 UTC - Liam: Initial hypothesis: telemetry scoring overweights 'recent_promotion' signal leading to premature routing to replicas still catching up KV cache.
03/10 06:40 UTC - SRE: Observed concurrent warmups on r-1012 and r-1078; both show low kv_warm progress and disk fallback latencies >100ms per shard.

03/11 09:12 UTC - Eng: Checked orchestration logs; autoscaler scheduled immediate promotion to meet capacity target during a rolling maintenance window—promotion routine did not wait for kv warmup by design.
03/11 14:02 UTC - Observability: Telemetry feature 'promotion_bias' has weight 0.85; kv_warmness metric is recorded but currently only used for monitoring not routing decisions.
03/12 11:48 UTC - Hypothesis validated by replay test: when promotion_bias is enabled, routing to recently promoted replicas increases p99 by 2.2x compared to routing with kv_warm filter applied.
resolution_notes: 2026-03-10 03:20 UTC - Temporary mitigation: Set telemetry.promote_bias=false for novalens-dedicated-1 (avoided routing to recently promoted replicas); p99 fell back to baseline within 20 minutes.

2026-03-12 17:30 UTC - Hotfix deployed to smart-routing: treat kv_warm==false as immediate disqualifier for full-traffic routing. Hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/orchestration/pull/220
Follow-up: Implement handshake during promotion to mark replica ready only after kv_warm_progress > 80% or after a successful in-memory KV preload. Owner: Liam Chen. ETA: 2026-03-20.
Runbook updates: Added section to 'KV Cache Warmup Policy' and 'Telemetry Routing' pages; included steps for manual rollback and emergency flag toggles.
comments: 2026-03-10 02:30 - Ava Martinez (Support): Customer Novalens reports long interactive latencies; triaging now. Please gather routing trace headers and active replica ids.
2026-03-10 03:25 - Liam Chen (SRE): Applied temporary config to disable promotion bias for Novalens cluster. Monitoring impact, will report back in 15m.
2026-03-10 03:50 - Novalens Ops (customer): Thanks — latency dropped noticeably after your change. Are we at risk of underutilization?
2026-03-11 09:20 - Priya Nair (Serving Eng): Confirmed hotfix PR to disqualify kv_warm==false; adding unit tests for routing policy. Assigned to Liam for rollout coordination.

2026-03-12 18:00 - Liam Chen (SRE): Hotfix merged and deployed to canary; observed no regressions in canary traffic. Scheduling deploy to Novalens cluster tomorrow morning with brief maintenance window.
